root.claim: One deterministic multitape Turing machine with a fixed alphabet and a fixed number of tapes multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, so no eventual $\Omega(n\log n)$ lower bound holds in this model.

motivation.text: Merely scanning $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so beating $n\log n$ requires savings in both data movement and butterfly arithmetic.

adds.name: saving exponent
adds.meaning: The fixed exponent $2^{-182}$ by which the logarithmic factor is reduced.

root.salient: The saving is a fixed power of the logarithm, uniform over all input lengths, beating the $n\log n$ bound that Harvey and van der Hoeven reached and that Schönhage and Strassen conjectured optimal in exactly this model.
